html:
Single-planet distance readout replacement

The user requested removal and replacement of the cluttered distance display, leading to the planet in the scene. The previous isolation test established that separate destination instances contributed the two number lines. The user also reported that the remaining readout looked jumbled.

The intended replacement targets the loaded BP_Planet_1 actor in NewMap. Its saved object name is BP_Planet_1_C_UAID_701CE7E4608772BA02_1615562978. Component widget setup will check its owner's exact name before creating a marker and use local player controller index 0. Other planet actors and their physical properties are preserved; their navigation components will not create additional markers. Renaming or recreating the target actor requires updating this explicit target.

The widget's distance binding will read the existing live Distance to Player, convert centimetres to kilometres, and format through native Conv_DoubleToText with grouping and at most one fraction digit. The single line is Planet: 1,680,092.8 km. The old separate destination-title field will be collapsed. World projection, the icon, the existing 30 Hz timer and pawn distance calculation are retained. This does not add collision avoidance for multiple destination labels.

Both saved Blueprints were copied and SHA-256 verified under OnTheGoNav/Saved/ForgeRepairs/PlanetReadout-20261012/ before any asset edits:

  • Widget: e013b585fd0e9d17cc03b0ebc9fcf6e8f2ceb7f70196c3588d1a11e5c82b748b.
  • Component: 2315714e2ad3da88cc55d1a3fc8e21df985239d2ee757791f362784e13aaac2d.

Server 0.3.4 and native bridge 0.2.10 add exact-GUID removal of bounded native graph nodes (excluding events, tunnels, graph terminators and structural nodes), with original node objects retained through compilation and reinstated before snapshot rollback on failure. These removals require explicit task authorization and a separate binary asset backup. The recovery journal alone is not that backup. Five exact pure native read/format functions are allowlisted: component GetOwner, GetObjectName, GetPlayerController, Conv_DoubleToText and Conv_TextToString. No general execution interface is introduced.

Four typed edit recipes are staged in Saved/PlanetReadoutRebuild/: replacement formatting, two bounded cleanup batches removing 53 obsolete formatting nodes, and single-target setup replacing controller enumeration. At this checkpoint these recipes passed Python schema validation and were applied in unreal-31644. Python regression: 307 passed. Ruff passed. Full Editor build linked successfully. The native removal/recovery and precision test passed with exit code 0 in the disposable host. Two earlier launches failed because the test Blueprint was not fully initialized; that fixture was corrected before the passing run. Evidence is retained in Saved/PlanetBridge0210/NativeTestsFinal/ and native-final.log. The tested bridge was installed after the user saved and closed OnTheGoNav. Its DLL SHA-256 is f807af568d682afd11b9f627fdfd8f56ef706889aaf2d407d85e42d9df29910c.

All four live edits completed with zero compiler errors and warnings. Final inspection verified 55 removed nodes (53 formatting nodes and two controller-loop nodes), 14 new/rewired connections in both directions, the collapsed title field and removal of its Visibility binding. The repaired distance graph contains 17 nodes, including four unused return nodes retained because graph terminators are outside the removal allowlist. Widget setup contains 16 nodes. The functional distance path has one valid return and one invalid-parent fallback. Existing unrelated graphs and scene actor transforms were preserved. The user save and flight test completed for the kilometre version: the user reported it looks good so far and requested a space-game unit presentation. Both repaired packages were saved, with hashes ab13c4e366a32e206d03b3268eb5d140e10da0f6770c86464cdc789b04d7d174 (widget) and 83b23f2f1a1856892e586b397b7f425fe92da7cac0a3d0619e4f9fdd70d30e9a (component). The latest completed Play run logged no Accessed None or division errors; it did log an unrelated duplicate Dodge animation-slot warning.

Space-game unit presentation

The subsequent formatting edit keeps the single target and live distance source, and selects unit, divisor and maximum fraction digits together:

Raw distance Presentation Maximum fraction digits
Below 1 km metres (m) 0
1 km to below 1,000 km kilometres (km) 1
1,000 km and above light-seconds (ls) 7

One light-second is 299,792.458 km, derived from the exact speed of light 299,792,458 m/s in the [BIPM metre definition](http[local path]). The raw centimetre divisor is therefore 29,979,245,800. The initial four-decimal presentation meant approximately 29.98-kilometre display steps, which hid normal flight movement. The final seven-decimal presentation uses approximately 29.98-metre steps. The example old readout 1,680,092.834 km becomes approximately Planet: 5.6041865 ls. Earlier conversational estimates of 30 metres for four decimals and 3 centimetres for seven were incorrect; these are corrected here.

The kilometre-only widget was backed up before this edit under Saved/ForgeRepairs/SpaceReadout-20261012/ in the target project. The typed edit added eight pure native selection nodes and 14 connections. Live apply compiled with zero errors and warnings; fresh inspection confirmed all 14 links in both directions. Eight boundary/sample cases were checked by interpreting the inspected graph's selection pins and constants; this is an offline structural/numeric check, not live UFunction invocation. Evidence is in Saved/SpaceReadoutRepair/. The initial four-decimal widget was saved with SHA-256 984938822f878212940655574187ee869bc2f075f7e663dc96499efb978982fb. The user reported that version was clear but its numbers did not move. The existing 1e14-cm component clamp remains; no interstellar-range support is claimed.

Precision correction and final acceptance

A reviewed edit changed the distant-unit precision selector from four to seven decimal places. A temporary log-only probe sampled the single active destination's live raw distance. The 54.502-second flight run produced 1,633 samples with 1,618 distinct raw values, spanning 168009064214.688049 to 168009284215.21317 cm. All samples round to one displayed value at four decimal places in light-seconds; seven decimal places produce 75 distinct displayed values. The user confirmed that the readout moves. The latest run logged no Accessed None or division errors.

After the run, four diagnostic nodes were removed through reviewed native edits and the direct refresh execution chain was restored. Precision, probe setup and cleanup all compiled with zero errors and warnings. Final native inspection verified the diagnostic nodes are absent and the original refresh link is present. The user saved the widget and confirmed the final component cleanup was saved. Final disk hashes:

  • Widget: 0844e56d2532a1862a0428d365fe28b48626641721398cc8b71f5c520378fd91.
  • Component: 8834436ede762f2697283e51232bd7529dcfe428563475037c0e5656151e7ece.

Pre-edit packages are backed up under the target project's Saved/ForgeRepairs/SpacePrecision-20261012/. Recipes, previews, apply responses, cleanup inspection and runtime verification are retained in [local path]. No native plugin source change or rebuild was needed for this precision correction.
